newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Jet set to plunge as summer nears.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Jet set to plunge as summer nears.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel prices are set for a free-fall as demand waned ahead of the north Asian summer sometime in June, traders said on Monday.
They expect jet prices to be on par with and even dip below gas oil during the peak of summer as was seen in previous years.
Jet prices started its unabated fall since February 19 when it was assessed at $28.80 a barrel.
Swaps gas oil was traded on Monday at $26.60 a barrel for March, down from Friday's $27.00, with the jet/gas oil regrade narrowing to $1.50/$1.80 from Friday's $1.60/$1.85.
The physical jet/gas oil spread was seen around $2.00, and was also set to narrow. Two offers were seen at $27.20 and $27.35 per barrel for March lifting, with no bids seen.
A deal was heard done on Friday between a Dutch trader and a Japanese trader at $27.80 free-on-board (fob) basis.

Traders said not much support was expected from Indonesia which has largely covered its March jet fuel requirements through purchases from a European major on an fob basis and from a MidEast oil firm on a cost-and-freight basis.
Gas oil also fell on fears that India might not buy much additional cargoes for April delivery after buying the less-than-expected volume of 570,000 tonnes in its first tender.
The lower crude and gas oil futures in London also pressured the Singapore market. But traders said physical and swaps gas oil were getting good support at $25.00.

An offer was seen at $25.20 a barrel, with a bid from a U.S. trader at $24.50 for March lifting. Another bid was seen from a European major at a 10-cent-per-barrel premium to Singapore spot quotes for March 7-26 lifting fob.
Swaps gas oil for March was traded as low as $24.95 a barrel and was last quoted at $25.00/$25.10, 20 cents below Friday's close.
